messages:
Maya: Heads up — starting a small 'strip-and-stitch' tranche this quarter to reduce coupling between request-router and enrichment hot paths. Posting the quick plan here; will follow up with a short RFC.
Ashish: Nice. Can you paste the sequence and the expected rollback points? thinking about KV cache ownership and session affinity.
Maya: High-level sequence: 1) add a thin facade API on router that normalizes enrichment calls, 2) route enrichment traffic through a non-blocking sidecar queue (async), 3) introduce user_profile_enriched store and backfill via streaming, 4) flip router to prefer cached enriched results, 5) pay down telemetry & tracing hooks, 6) run canary -> widen. Rollback points are the feature flags at steps 2 & 4.
Ben: +1 for async. Main tradeoff is eventual consistency for enrichments that used to be sync. For small number of endpoints we should keep a short-circuit sync path behind a FF.
Irene: SLO concern — async fanout can increase tail latency if queue backs up. What are the throttle and circuit-breaker plans?
Maya: We'll provision a dedicated queue with per-tenant quotas and a token-bucket throttle. Circuit-breaker behavior: after N failures queue drops to fallback path and router will serve best-effort cached results. We'll have a telemetry guardrail: if tail latency > X ms or error rate > Y, FF auto-flips.
Lucy: Customer impact? Which tenants move first?
Maya: Start with internal tenants and low-traffic PLG tier. Enterprise tenants will be scheduled after the backfill completes and we validate regression metrics.
Ben: DB migration note: denormalize into user_profile_enriched table, write-path dual-writes during migration, backfill via changefeed. Keep migration idempotent and resumable.
Ashish: Interface boundary: facade API should be stable and only accept compact payloads (id, feature-flags, ctx). No business logic in facade — enrichment logic stays in the sidecar service.
Maya: Agreed. Also adding a small compatibility shim on the router for older clients for two sprints.
Irene: For canary/rollback, we should add synthetic traces every minute and an alert pipeline that watches sampling rate, p99, and queue depth per shard.
Maya: I'll add those to the SRE checklist. Also planning a small chaos experiment to validate graceful degradation.
ops-bot: deploy queued — canary feature-flag rollout requested by @Maya. (simulated)
Ben: Quick config sample for FF gating:
```
feature_flags:
  enrichment_async: {
    rollout_percentage: 5,
    rollback_on: ["p99_latency>1200ms", "error_rate>0.5%"]
  }
```
Maya: I'll draft the RFC follow-up doc and link the migration runbook. Owners: @Ben for DB migration, @Irene for SLOs/alerts, @Ashish for API facade, @Maya for rollout coordination. :thumbsup:
Lucy: Thanks — please add a short customer comms blurb in the RFC so support has context.
Maya: Will do. Short action items: make RFC, create runbook, add FF & metrics, schedule canary window. Meeting next Wed to confirm owners and dates.
